question: Can the monastic reform documented epigraphically under Parakramabahu I be connected to the unusually productive grammatical and Pali intellectual programme of the same reform era?
mechanism: Institutional unification and discipline created a reformed scholarly community in which textual standardisation and new grammatical tools could help reproduce a shared learned tradition; Gornall's intellectual history treats grammar as part of that reform process rather than an unrelated courtly by-product.
transmission_channel: monastic regulation, scholarly training, textual standardisation and teacher-pupil lineages
time_lag: contemporaneous to multi-decade within the 1157-1270 reform era
scale: Z1 institutional reform to Z2 intellectual network
confounders: political instability rather than stability as an alternative stimulus
royal reform rhetoric versus lived monastic practice
bounded_by: Supports a reform-to-textual-production mechanism, not a deterministic claim that royal regulation directly caused each grammar or that all Pali scholarship depended on one institutional centre.
